facts: PDF 5 title identifies the Ordo Sabbati Sancti quando Vigilia Paschalis instaurata peragitur, TPV, MDCCCCLI (1951).
PDF 7 / printed 5 decree has 9 February 1951 dateline, Micara and Carinci signatures; local-Ordinary discretion and an experiment for that year, not a permanent whole-missal replacement.
PDF 9 / printed 7 is the Office component. PDF 10 / printed 8 gives the first new-fire prayer in full where AAS 131 references the existing missal instead.
PDF 11 / printed 9 includes the candle incision diagram with the 1951 digits and the processional chant notation. AAS prints the prescriptions but no corresponding sung notation.
PDF 36 / printed 34 contains the renewal of baptismal promises and the narrowly conditioned vernacular permission; compared against AAS 135-136.
PDF 39 / printed 37 prints the Mass opening and proper, whereas AAS 137 directs the reader to the existing missal except named changes.
PDF 41 / printed 39 ends the peculiar rubrics for the priest celebrating Easter Mass after the Vigil. PDF 42 is the index, PDF 43 blank, PDF 44 publisher advertisement.
Entire published decree and following rubrics read on rendered pages, with surrounding unrelated material excluded at the start of 128.
Decree begins on 128 and ends on 129, 9 February 1951; rubrics 130-137 comprise Office; Vigil with eight chapters; solemn Vigil Mass.
The AAS rubric text uses references to the existing Missal and therefore cannot substitute for every prayer, reading or musical content in the physical 1951 booklet.

Selected direct checks against the acquired booklet: decree/date; Office pp 130 / booklet 7; new-fire rule AAS 131 / booklet 8; candle incisions AAS 131-132 / booklet 8-9; renewal AAS 135-136 / booklet 34; Mass AAS 137 / booklet 37 and 39. No word-for-word whole-book collation is claimed.
Complete De rubricis ad simpliciorem formam redigendis read at printed/PDF 218-224; 225 begins the next AAS issue and is outside the act.
Dateline 23 March 1955 and commencement 1 January 1956 are distinct (p 219).
Title I general norms; Title II calendar changes; Title III commemorations; Title IV Breviary changes; Title V Missal changes. These cover more than Holy Week.

Title II pp 219-221 explicitly suppresses semidouble rank, most vigils and octaves except the enumerated survivals. Title V p 224 changes oration practice, the Dies irae condition, Credo, preface selection and the last Gospel.
This verifies the complete published act and named prescriptions, not a reconstructed operational Missal or a comparison of all before/after formularies.
Unpaginated publisher advertisement on the final PDF page identifies the separate Preces Eucharisticae et Praefationes as 54 pages, 17 x 24 cm.
Advertisement distinguishes three additional Eucharistic Prayers and associated prefaces, initial selection norms, rubricated liturgical printing, and Gregorian melody for the parts that may be sung.
The notice confirms why the periodical pp 156-179 cannot certify the separate booklet's entire physical and musical contents. No separate 54-page booklet acquired.

versions.qualification: Complete offered 44-page scan of the 1951 TPV experimental Ordo acquired. Original title, 9 February decree, selected Office/Vigil/Mass loci, final printed p. 39 and index inspected. Its physical service-book contents exceed the AAS rubrics, which refer back to the existing Missal. Exact scan and modern body remain withheld; no whole-text collation or ideal-edition completeness claim.

Own complete published act now image-read, AAS 47 (1955) 218-224, not merely cited in a later act. Five titles cover general norms, calendar, commemorations, Breviary and Missal; the Missal-specific prescriptions are at 224. Full operational Missal and exact before/after prayer collation remain unestablished.
